prisoner.name: Samuel Reynier Tyson
prisoner.description: Samuel Reynier Tyson was a California Quaker, farmer and peace organizer associated with the Committee for Nonviolent Action and the Fellowship of Reconciliation. He helped the Everyman anti-nuclear campaign and was imprisoned in 1962. His obituary records six months actually served.

cases.charges: Contempt of federal court order prohibiting the Everyman nuclear-test protest voyage
cases.sentence: Six-month contempt sentence in 1962; six months served according to his obituary. A contemporary Santa Rita letter reports his solitary confinement. Exact admission and release dates are unverified.

entries.custody_evidence: The five full names in the July sentencing report match Chaffee and his four named fellow prisoners in the August 22 Santa Rita letter. The letter describes ongoing imprisonment and repeated prison activities, not initial arrest processing.
entries.research_notes: No full-term service is inferred from the imposed six months. Boat numbering differs between accounts; the record uses Everyman without a numeral. No modern Santa Rita institution is substituted for the historical facility.

prisoner.name: Walter Chaffee
prisoner.description: Walter Chaffee was a California art instructor and participant in the CNVA Everyman voyage opposing nuclear tests. After imprisonment for contempt in 1962, he wrote from Santa Rita Jail about the five defendants and their continuing nonviolent witness in custody.

cases.charges: Contempt of federal court order prohibiting the Everyman nuclear-test protest voyage
cases.sentence: Sentenced to six months for contempt in July 1962. His August 22 letter confirms ongoing Santa Rita imprisonment. Total time served and release date are not established.

entries.custody_evidence: The five full names in the July sentencing report match Chaffee and his four named fellow prisoners in the August 22 Santa Rita letter. The letter describes ongoing imprisonment and repeated prison activities, not initial arrest processing.

prisoner.name: Barton Stone
prisoner.description: Barton Stone participated in the CNVA Everyman anti-nuclear voyage and was imprisoned at Santa Rita in 1962. He later described practicing Zen during his confinement and receiving a visit from Shunryu Suzuki.

cases.charges: Contempt of federal court order prohibiting the Everyman nuclear-test protest voyage
cases.sentence: The contemporary report gives a six-month contempt sentence; a later interview recalls a longer sentence and eight months held. Imprisonment is confirmed, but the conflicting duration is not entered as a counter.

prisoner.name: Robert Robbins
prisoner.description: Robert Robbins, a San Francisco picture framer, participated in the CNVA Everyman anti-nuclear voyage. He was imprisoned for contempt in 1962; a letter from his fellow prisoner identifies him among the defendants held at Santa Rita.

cases.charges: Contempt of federal court order prohibiting the Everyman nuclear-test protest voyage
cases.sentence: Sentenced to six months for contempt in July 1962; still held at Santa Rita in the August 22 prison letter. Exact admission and release dates and total time served remain unverified.

prisoner.name: Roger Moss
prisoner.description: Roger Moss helped organize the CNVA Everyman anti-nuclear voyage and was imprisoned for contempt in 1962. Walter Chaffee named him in a letter from Santa Rita Jail, describing their refusal to work on military projects while confined.
